thesis: Vertiv's ~14.5% 60-day decline traces to a confirmed, company-disclosed Q2 2026 earnings disappointment reported July 29, 2026 -- shares fell 17.3% that session on unexpected execution challenges scaling large-scale modular data-center deployments against a multi-year backlog management had called on-track as recently as the April Q1 call. Since then, however, Vertiv reaffirmed a raised FY2026 outlook (net sales guided to $13.8-14.2B, adjusted EPS $6.65-6.75, implying 30-32% organic growth) at its August 11 earnings call, and multiple sell-side firms (Bernstein, Mizuho, GLJ Research) issued fresh Buy ratings through August, even though a securities-law investigation (Hagens Berman, opened mid-August) into whether the April Q1 commentary was misleading about the same backlog/deployment issue remains open. This suggests the pullback reflects a real but so-far-contained execution stumble that management and analysts view as recoverable given still-strong AI data-center demand, rather than a structural deterioration in the underlying business.
invalidation: Invalidated if Q3 2026 results (expected ~November 2026) show the backlog/deployment execution issues from Q2 persisting or worsening, if the Hagens Berman investigation matures into a filed securities class action with disclosures suggesting management knowingly misled investors on the April Q1 call, or if AI data-center capex demand decelerates broadly.

thesis: Marvell's Q2 FY27 results reported Aug 27, 2026 beat consensus (revenue +37% YoY to $2.74B, data-center revenue growth accelerating to 46% YoY) and management raised FY2028 revenue guidance to ~$18B (from $16.5B), a confirmed company-disclosed catalyst. Shares nonetheless fell roughly 6% because the outlook fell short of expectations built up after a nearly 3x YTD run to a rich valuation. This suggests the pullback is primarily a valuation reset against genuinely strong and improving fundamentals rather than a company-specific negative development, though the newly disclosed Google custom-silicon warrant (up to 58.97M shares / ~$12.2B strike value, announced Aug 18-21, 2026, exercise price $206.58) is a real, freshly disclosed dilution overhang -- up to roughly 6-7% of shares outstanding if fully exercised as Google's purchases scale.
invalidation: Invalidated if Q3 FY27 results miss the raised guidance, if gross margins fall meaningfully below the guided trajectory, if Google's custom-silicon purchases and warrant vesting accelerate materially faster than shipment/revenue milestones imply, or if sector-wide AI-capex sentiment continues to compress the multiple independent of Marvell's own execution.

thesis: NVIDIA's ~11.7% 60-day rise is grounded in a confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst: fiscal Q2 FY2027 results reported Aug 26, 2026 showed $96.2B revenue with data-center revenue of $89B and operating margin at 65.2%, alongside fresh partnership disclosures the same week (AWS committing to 2 million additional GPUs; a deepened NVIDIA-MediaTek Edge-to-Cloud collaboration). This suggests continued, broadening AI-infrastructure demand is the primary driver rather than sentiment or a sector-wide rally alone. The read is complicated by two unresolved risks that don't currently carry a near-term binary trigger: a certified securities class action over 2017-2018 crypto-mining revenue disclosures (class certified March 25, 2026, most recent procedural conference April 21, 2026, no trial date yet set) and a long-running Chinese antitrust probe tied to Mellanox-deal compliance -- but neither has a scheduled ruling, hearing, or compliance deadline in the next ~90 days, and the crypto-mining case concerns disclosures from nearly a decade ago with no bearing on current operating fundamentals, so neither changes the near-term read.
invalidation: Invalidated if hyperscaler/AI-infrastructure capex growth decelerates materially in upcoming quarters, if a scheduled hearing or ruling emerges in either the crypto-mining class action or the China antitrust matter signaling material financial exposure, or if a future quarter breaks the pattern of guidance beats seen this year.

thesis: SpaceX shares have fallen roughly 12.7% over the past 60 days and are now about 39% below their June 16, 2026 all-time high. Q2 2026 results (reported Aug 4) showed capital expenditures surging more than sixfold to $18.4B (most of it AI-related) alongside a $541M net loss, and roughly 319M additional lockup shares became tradeable in late August as part of a staggered unlock covering ~88% of the company's 13B+ shares through 2027 -- both confirmed, company-specific developments that explain continued selling pressure rather than a market-wide rotation. Layered on top are several open legal matters without a clear near-term resolution: a Clean Air Act suit over gas-turbine permitting for the Colossus 2 data center that jeopardizes a $45B Anthropic compute agreement, a former-employee retaliation suit tied to 2022 firings, and a SpaceX-initiated suit against DOJ officials over hiring-discrimination allegations. None of these carries a scheduled ruling or hearing date in the next ~90 days, but combined with continued heavy cash burn and an unresolved profitability timeline, the balance of confirmed negative developments still outweighs the case for entering here.
invalidation: Thesis would need reassessment if the Colossus 2 Clean Air Act dispute is resolved without disrupting the Anthropic compute agreement, if Q3 2026 results show a credible narrowing of cash burn without further large dilutive events, or if the stock stabilizes well above its IPO price with lockup-related selling pressure clearly abating.

thesis: Intel's ~25.7% 60-day decline coincides with a confirmed, company-disclosed dilutive event: an upsized $20B common-stock offering priced Aug 10-18, 2026 at $95/share (210.5M new shares, up from an initial $15B target), on top of continuing Intel Foundry operating losses ($2.8B in Q2 2026 alone, guided to exceed $10B cumulative through 2027) and x86 server share continuing to erode to AMD (now near 34% server share). These are real, disclosed structural pressures rather than a rumor or macro move. A partial offset is that Tiger Global added to its Intel stake in Q2 2026, and a Delaware Court of Chancery derivative suit challenging the government's 10% equity stake (filed March 2026) remains open with no ruling or hearing scheduled in the next ~90 days per available reporting, so it isn't treated as a near-term binary risk. On balance the evidence remains mixed -- real fresh dilution and continuing Foundry losses against one large institutional buyer and no imminent litigation catalyst -- rather than clearly resolved in either direction.
invalidation: Thesis would need reassessment if Intel Foundry demonstrates a credible path to breakeven meaningfully ahead of the 2027 guided timeline, if x86 server share losses to AMD stabilize, or if the Delaware derivative suit over the government stake produces a ruling materially affecting Intel's capital structure.

thesis: AMD's ~10.1% 60-day decline (just past the signal threshold) coincides with a broad Philadelphia Semiconductor Index selloff (down 3.5% the same session) tied to rate-driven rotation out of high-growth chip names, not any AMD-specific negative disclosure -- Q2 2026 results were record ($6.7B+ data-center revenue, more than doubling YoY) and no litigation, accounting, or executive-conduct issue was found for AMD in this cycle's research. The OpenAI/Meta compute-for-equity warrants (up to 320M shares combined) were disclosed back in February 2026, more than 90 days ago, so they are not treated as a fresh dilution-risk flag this cycle even though they remain a longer-run overhang tied to $600 share-price vesting milestones. Because the move is explained as macro/sector-wide rather than company-specific, this is scored low regardless of AMD's otherwise strong underlying results.
invalidation: Thesis is invalidated if Q3 2026 earnings (due ~Nov 2026) show decelerating data-center/AI revenue growth or margin compression, if a new SEC/DOJ inquiry or securities suit naming AMD specifically is disclosed, or if the stock's decline is later found to trace to an AMD-specific issue rather than the broader semiconductor rate-driven selloff.

thesis: Dell's ~15.7% 60-day rise is grounded in a confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst: Dell was named technology provider on a $10B AI-factory deal with AI cloud startup Volta (disclosed Aug 4, 2026), part of a broader run that has taken the stock up roughly 250%+ over six months on record AI-server backlog and demand. No litigation, accounting restatement, dilutive raise, insolvency signal, or operationally-driven leadership departure was found in this cycle's research -- Dell's only recent corporate-structure change was a routine Texas redomestication effective July 1, 2026, and historical governance issues (a 2018 Class V stockholder settlement, a 2006-07 accounting matter) are well outside the 3-year lookback. Dell reports Q2 FY27 earnings on September 1, 2026 -- literally the next trading day -- a live, unresolved binary event that could confirm or reverse the current backlog-conversion read, which is why conviction is capped at medium rather than high.
invalidation: A material miss on Q2 FY27 revenue/EPS or AI-server backlog/guidance versus consensus, disclosed at or after the September 1, 2026 earnings report, or evidence that supply constraints are preventing backlog-to-revenue conversion.

thesis: Sunbelt Rentals' 10.7x volume spike on Aug 31, 2026 doesn't trace to one clear new company-specific catalyst in this cycle's research -- available reporting points to a mix of an already-known Wells Fargo Overweight initiation (Aug 17), an ongoing $1.5B buyback, and routine board additions (effective Aug 1), none dated to the spike itself, against a backdrop of an active federal antitrust MDL alleging Sunbelt, United Rentals, Herc, H&E, and Sunstate coordinated rental pricing through the Rouse data platform (filed April 2025, still in active proceedings with no scheduled ruling found) and continued sector pressure from soft nonresidential construction spending that drove JPMorgan/BofA price-target cuts earlier in the quarter. With no confirmed single catalyst behind today's volume and both a sector-wide construction-spending headwind and an unresolved antitrust overhang in play, this reads as largely mechanical/sentiment-driven rather than a fundamental resolution, and Q1 FY2027 earnings (Sept 9, 2026) remain a pending, unresolved catalyst.
invalidation: Thesis would need reassessment if Q1 FY2027 results (Sept 9, 2026) show margin stabilization and volume/rate reacceleration, nonresidential construction spending data turns positive, or the antitrust MDL is dismissed with prejudice as to Sunbelt.
